title: Deployment economics experiments — license mix & TCO slices
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is an experiments sheet for comparing on-prem vs VPC private deployment economics across small-medium-large customer archetypes. Focus is on: 1) how to present licensing + support bundle combinations, 2) TCO slices that make the decision intuitive to finance teams, and 3) sensitivity breakpoints where on-prem becomes cheaper than VPC depending on utilization, amortization period, and discounting.

High-level approach (notes):
- Decompose costs into three orthogonal slices: Capital (HW), Recurrent infra (cloud/GPU hours), and Platform (license + support). Treat security/compliance uplift as a delta on Platform costs.
- Show both upfront CAPEX amortized (straight-line) and an OPEX-first view (lease equivalent) to match customer accounting preferences.
- Provide small, medium, large scenario templates with plug-in knobs: sustained GPU utilization %, average seq len, peak QPS, replication factor, expected growth rate.
- Offer 3 bundle examples: Basic (software only, community model tuning), Pro (license + standard support + 90-day security patches), Enterprise (license + 24/7 support + prioritized rollouts + on-site assistance).

Assumptions (base case) — keep a live table in sheet tabs:
- Amortization window: 3 years (default), alternate scenarios: 2, 5 years.
- HW list price (per node): $35,000 (A100-ish equivalent), usable nodes per cluster: 8, redundancy factor 1.2 (for maintenance).
- Effective hourly cost if on-prem treated as leased: $1.60/hr per GPU (includes power, rack, ops).
- Cloud VPC private nodes: $3.10/hr per GPU (net of committed discounts).
- License fee: Basic $0/yr, Pro $150k/yr, Enterprise $450k/yr (covers access to Redwood private repo, secure builds, support).
- Support uplift: Basic 0%, Pro 12% of license, Enterprise 30% of license (for SLA & 24/7).
- Network egress + connectivity for VPC: $1.5k/month baseline for customer-managed transit.
- Headcount for customer ops (on-prem): 0.2 FTE per 10 nodes (salaries fully burdened $160k/yr).
- Depreciation/tax: Not modeled here — leave as a configurable input (finance prefers to use their schedule).

Sample scenario matrix (tabular excerpt for quick read):

Scenario | GPUs needed | Utilization | Amortization | On-prem annual cost | VPC annual cost | Delta (VPC - Onprem)
Small  | 16 | 40% | 3y | $675,400 | $889,000 | +$213,600
Medium | 64 | 60% | 3y | $1,920,800 | $2,280,000 | +$359,200
Large  | 256 | 75% | 3y | $6,800,000 | $7,864,000 | +$1,064,000

Note: these numbers include HW amortization, licenses (Pro by default), baseline ops FTE, and network costs.

Key insights from quick sweeps:
- Utilization sensitivity is the dominant lever. On-prem becomes strongly favorable when sustained utilization > ~55% for medium/large scale given our HW price assumptions.
- Short amortization windows (2y) tilt in favor of VPC unless customer has very high utilization or strong tax amortization benefits.
- License mix matters: small customers often prefer Pro or Basic. Enterprise license as a percentage of total spend drops with scale, improving on-prem relative attractiveness.
- Support bundling can be used to smooth revenue: convert a large upfront discount into a multi-year support commitment.

Experiment #A: License as capacity hedge (new idea)
- Offer a blended bundle: upfront discount on license if customer commits to usage bands (e.g., commit to 12 months of 75% average capacity). If they exceed, they pay incremental token/usage overage.
- Rationale: reduces sticker shock for on-prem procurements and converts uncertain HW ops spend into predictable platform revenue.
- Experiment inputs to model: commit band, overage floor, step pricing for overages, true-up cadence (quarterly).

Experiment #B: Support-included amortization smoothing
- Present an integrated price where the license is amortized (customer sees a single recurring charge). This is useful for procurement that wants OPEX-only contracts.
- Model outcome: moves on-prem into parity for customers that cannot take CAPEX.

Quick sensitivity tables (placeholders to include in sheet):
1) Break-even utilization by amortization window: 2y: ~70%, 3y: ~56%, 5y: ~42% (approx).
2) Break-even license level: with license waived (Basic), on-prem wins sooner (lower capex hurdle).
3) Effect of headcount: +0.1 FTE per 10 nodes increases on-prem TCO by ~3–4% depending on salary assumptions.

Representative calculations (show in sheet as formula notes):
- On-prem HW annualized = (num_gpus/GPUs_per_node * node_price * redundancy)/amort_years + ops_FTE_costs + power_and_amenities
- VPC annualized = num_gpus * hrs_per_year * vpc_hourly_rate + network + license + support
- Hrs per year baseline = 24 * 365 * utilization

Sections to include in the sheet (tab names suggested):
- README (this doc)
- Inputs & knobs (all assumptions as editable cells)
- Scenario bank (small/medium/large + custom)
- Sensitivity sweeps (utilization, amort window, license levels)
- Bundle catalog (text table of what Basic/Pro/Enterprise covers)
- Sales pitch appendix (how to present to finance — sample email + 1-slide summary)
- Open questions & decisions log

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Confirm up-to-date HW list prices with infra purchasing (Ethan). Current numbers are conservative 2025 list.
- Validate effective VPC committed discounts with Sales Ops (Maya). We need realistic committed SKU pricing for private clusters — current $3.10/hr is an average of multiple partners and may be off.
- Decide default license allocation for scenarios (Pro used here as default; maybe Basic is more common for SMB in sales funnel).
- Tax treatment: how to present CAPEX vs OPEX to CFOs in different geos (EMEA vs US). Suggest a small appendix with 2 tax profiles.

Recommended next experiments (near-term):
1) Build a customer-facing 1-pager that shows a single line TCO comparison with toggles for amortization window and utilization. Prefer interactive widget for sales demo.
2) Run historical cluster telemetry through model to compute realized utilization distributions across 12 pilot customers — gives empirical breakpoints.
3) Pilot a blended license commitment: one customer willing to try on a 12-month commit with true-up. Run pricing experiment with 10% discount + 20% overage margin.

Presentation templates (short):
- Finance one-liner: "On-prem break-even at X GPUs and Y% sustained utilization over N years. For your declared workload, we estimate net saving of $Z over 36 months."
- Procurement bullet points: list of items included in Enterprise bundle, 3-year support SLAs, replacement lead times, warranty terms, and upgrade path for GPUs.

Draft messaging for sales playbook (copyable):
- If the buyer expects sustained usage above 50% and cares about unit economics over 3+ years -> lead with on-prem ROI analysis.
- If buyer is constrained to OPEX-only -> propose amortized license + managed VPC or lease-equivalent.
- For risk-averse security buyers -> show VPC private + Redwood-managed control plane as fallback for initial rollout, then propose an on-prem migration when usage stabilizes.

Action items (owners):
- Ethan: get procurement HW quotes + rack space/colocation baseline by 2026-01-15.
- Maya: validate partner VPC per-GPU committed rates and provide 3 representative quotes by 2025-11-20.
- Priya: build the interactive 1-pager demo and mock for sales by 2026-02-01.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the sheet lightweight for sales demos; heavy math can live on a hidden tab.
- We should consider offering a "migration credit" when a customer shifts from VPC to on-prem (to avoid churn).
- Important to align with legal on what counts as "support included" vs chargeable professional services.

Revision log: 
- 2025-10-03 Priya created initial draft with base assumptions.
- 2025-11-01 Ethan added early procurement notes.
- 2026-02-18 Maya updated VPC rates after partner calls.

End of doc — add to sheet tabs and iterate.
